recipe: Experimental React only: `<Suspense defer fallback={...}>` lets React show the fallback first and render/stream expensive children later even if nothing suspends. Not available in stable React; do not use it in stable-release code.
trigger_condition: Your Suspense boundary wraps content that is computationally expensive to render and you want to show the fallback before the full render completes.
evidence: When `true`, React may show the `fallback` first and render or stream `children` later, even when nothing in them suspends. Use it for content that is expensive to render.
_original_recipe: Pass `defer={true}` to a Suspense boundary when the children are expensive to render, so React shows the fallback first and streams the content in later.

trigger_condition: When you want different parts of your UI to load and reveal independently rather than all at once.
evidence: This lets you nest multiple Suspense components to create a loading sequence. Each Suspense boundary's fallback will be filled in as the next level of content becomes available.

recipe: Wrap data-loading components in an intermediate component without changing Suspense behavior, as long as they share the same closest parent Suspense boundary.
trigger_condition: When you want to restructure your component hierarchy for code organization without affecting how Suspense coordinates loading.
evidence: Components that load data don't have to be direct children of the Suspense boundary. For example, you can move `Biography` and `Albums` into a new `Details` component. This doesn't change the behavior.

recipe: Keep Suspense boundaries at the level of the loading sequence the user should experience, not around every individual component.
trigger_condition: When deciding where to place Suspense boundaries in your component tree.
evidence: Don't put a Suspense boundary around every component. Suspense boundaries should not be more granular than the loading sequence that you want the user to experience.

recipe: Add a `key` prop to the `<Suspense>` boundary or a component above it that changes with the navigated content (e.g., the user ID) so React resets the boundary and shows the fallback instead of stale previous content.
trigger_condition: You are navigating between different content (e.g., different user profiles) and want the Suspense fallback to appear instead of showing the previous content while new content loads.
evidence: With a different `key`, React treats the profiles as different content and resets the Suspense boundary during navigation. The `key` can go on the boundary itself or on a component above it.

New API (React 19.3 canary era); check your react-dom exports it, else throw on the server instead.
trigger_condition: A component uses browser-only APIs such as `localStorage` and you need a visible fallback in the initial server-rendered HTML before hydration completes.
evidence: A Suspense boundary can provide a fallback for a browser-only component. Wrap the component in `<Suspense>` and call [`use(browser())`](/reference/react/use#use-browser) inside it.

recipe: Render stylesheets using `<link rel="stylesheet">` with a `precedence` prop inside your suspended component to make the Suspense boundary wait for the stylesheet before revealing content.
trigger_condition: You want a Suspense boundary to block until a stylesheet has loaded so content doesn't appear unstyled.
evidence: A stylesheet rendered with [`<link rel="stylesheet">` and a `precedence` prop](/reference/react-dom/components/link#special-rendering-behavior) blocks the Suspense boundary until the stylesheet loads, up to a timeout, so the content doesn't appear unstyled.

recipe: When a `<ViewTransition>` animates a Suspense reveal, React waits (up to a timeout) for fonts the new content introduces, avoiding a fallback-font flash. This only happens during a ViewTransition update; requires a React version that exports ViewTransition.
trigger_condition: Your Suspense content introduces new fonts and you want to avoid the fallback font flash on reveal.
evidence: When a [`<ViewTransition>`](/reference/react/ViewTransition) animates a Suspense boundary's reveal, React waits for new fonts the content introduces, up to a timeout, so the text doesn't flash with a fallback font. This only happens during a `<ViewTransition>` update.
_original_recipe: To prevent text from flashing with a fallback font when Suspense content reveals, wrap the Suspense boundary in a `<ViewTransition>` so React waits for new fonts to load before revealing the content.
